fix: Both ctrls now hold the temporaries in crate::runtime::mem::CleansedScratch, whose Drop wipes the whole buffer with the volatile CLEANSE primitive. Construction precedes every early return, so every path - success, refusal-before-secret, and mid-computation failure - cleanses each temporary exactly once.

The explicit success-path OPENSSL_cleanse emulations (write_bytes over sha1tmp; write_bytes over md5tmp and sha1tmp) were removed; a single Drop now owns the obligation. This also covers padtmp, which the success path previously left untouched.
CleansedScratch gained a safe fill(byte) method for the pad_1 (0x36) and pad_2 (0x5c) fills. This is additive; the type's Drop contract is unchanged.

A test-only observer module (runtime::mem::cleanse_hooks) records each Drop while the owner's storage is still live: length, non-zero byte count before the wipe, and that every byte reads zero after it. Release builds carry none of it.

A test-only failure arm at each ctrl's reinitialisation (sha1::test_hooks::set_fail_reinit, md5_sha1::test_hooks::set_fail_init) makes the early-failure return after the intermediates were written reachable without invalid input. The reinitialisation itself still runs as before; only the returned verdict is overridden in test builds.
digest_mathematics_unchanged: No Update/Final call, argument, padding byte, digest length or return value changed. The ctrls' ctrl return values (-2, 0, 1) and their conditions are unchanged; the failure hooks are #[cfg(test)] only and do not alter release control flow.

eliminated: One explicit unsafe write_bytes cleanse block in ossl_sha1_ctrl and one in ossl_md5_sha1_ctrl; both are replaced by the safe CleansedScratch Drop.
unsafe_accounting.note: The Drop's existing single unsafe cleanse operation is unchanged; the new fill method and the test hooks add no unsafe.
